nisar_acquisition_environment.blocker_explanation: 1) Matched same-track, same-frame pre-fire (Provisional CRID P05023, July/Sept 2026) and post-fire (Provisional CRID P05023 August/Oct 2026 + Validated CRID P05036 Oct 2026) NISAR L2 GCOV pairs were discovered in live NASA CMR across all 4 wildfire events. 2) Full-frame HDF5 downloads require 51.49 GB for the 4 primary pairs (exceeding the 12.53 GB local disk budget -> BLOCKED_STORAGE). 3) NASA Harmony OGC API Coverages supports server-side spatial + variable subsetting (reducing the 4 primary pairs to ~20.48 MB total, easily fitting local storage), but both Harmony and ASF Earthdata Cloud return HTTP 302/303 redirects to https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov/oauth/authorize and require NASA Earthdata Login credentials (~/.netrc or EARTHDATA_USERNAME/EARTHDATA_PASSWORD/EARTHDATA_TOKEN), which are not present in this environment -> BLOCKED_AUTH.

scientific_limitations_and_disclaimers: Every model uses Sentinel-1 C-band input and Sentinel-2-derived labels; this is a cross-sensor prototype, not a NISAR result.
Only three events contribute to experiments (one TRAIN, one VAL, one TEST), so generalisation estimates have very high variance.
The TEST event (Bug Fire) has a much larger burned fraction than TRAIN (Gann Fire); class prior shift is severe.
MCD64A1 and the dNBR reference disagree substantially for the TEST event; burned-area labels are uncertain, not ground truth.
Sentinel-1 valid-data fraction for the TEST event is about 0.73 because of the swath edge, which further limits the test domain.
CUSUM is unsupervised and uses only the first acquisition as its baseline; it is not directly comparable to supervised segmentation.
Pixel metrics are spatially autocorrelated; blocked-bootstrap intervals are reported but still reflect only one test event.
